summary: Lemma (verified exactly on all 7.8·10⁶ pairs (p,C), p≤10⁶, C≤200): the number of divisors d≡−1 (mod 4C) of 4Cp+1 is odd iff 4Cp+1 is a square s² with s≡−1 (mod 4C) (involution d↔N/d). Hence R(p)=Σ_C L_C(p) is always even and the parity is forced only at square levels. The natural non-forced quantity is the half-count H(p)=R(p)/2: its parity is balanced (19571 odd vs 19603 even, p≤10⁶; scripts/z52d_p2_TO8_Z2990.py). So the naive parity is trivial and the non-trivial parity is free.

summary: Norm compatibility across levels C | C′ fails for an elementary reason: if d | 4C′p+1 and d | 4Cp+1, then d divides (4C′p+1) − (C′/C)(4Cp+1) = 1 − C′/C, so a certificate divisor at level C′ can share a factor with level C only when d | (C′/C − 1), a bounded set. The 'obstruction group' compatibility is therefore trivial at the level of divisors (argument; no table computed).
